figures.caption: Figure 1: Brain alignment across the cortical hierarchy for human (left) and macaque (right). Lines show Spearman ρ between model and neural RDMs per learning rule. Shaded bands: bootstrap 95% CI (N = 10,000). Grey hatched band: noise ceiling (Spearman–Brown corrected split-half). Macaque ρ values are substantially higher than human, reflecting the higher SNR of electrophysiology. STDP and PC lead at macaque V1/V2. Note: the macaque panel combines two datasets—FreemanZiemba2013 (textures) for V1/V2 and MajajHong2015 (HVM objects) for V4/IT. The sharp V2→V4 drop is confounded by this dataset switch (see text).

Figure 2: Cross-species ranking comparison. Each panel shows human ρ (x-axis) vs. macaque ρ (y-axis) per learning rule at one brain region. Kendall’s τ with exact p-values from exhaustive permutation over all 5! = 120 orderings. At n = 5, only τ = ±1.0 can reach significance at α = 0.05. All macaque points lie above the identity line, reflecting the electrophysiology SNR advantage.
Figure 3: V1 alignment per learning rule, grouped by species. Human ∆ρ = 0.064; macaque ∆ρ = 0.147. Electrophysiology resolves larger differences between learning rules at V1 than fMRI.

Figure 4: Species × learning rule interaction effects. Values show (∆ρhuman−∆ρmacaque) where ∆ρ = ρrule−ρrandom. Negative values (blue): macaque benefits more from the learning rule than human. STDP and PC show strong negative interactions at V1/V2.

Figure 5: Architecture comparison: custom 3-conv CNN (5 learning rules) vs. pretrained ResNet-50. At V1/V2, ResNet-50 performs comparably to BP/FA but below STDP/PC. At IT, ResNet-50 (ρ ≈ 0.25) dramatically outperforms all CNN conditions (ρ = 0.07–0.14), suggesting that IT alignment scales with model capacity and training data. Macaque error bars: mean ± std across 5 seeds. †STDP IT uses n = 4 seeds (seed-0 lacked FC1 weights; see Section 3.1).

Figure 6: Stimulus control: are learning-rule rankings stable across stimulus sets? Each panel shows model ρ on THINGS-720 (human stimuli, x-axis) vs. model ρ on macaque stimuli (y-axis). Rankings are moderately stable at V1 (τ = 0.40) but weakly inverted at IT (τ = −0.40), suggesting that cross-species IT differences may be partially driven by stimulus domain.
